ideas.description: Replace the template recipe in submissions/arena/ with an airbench96-style port. Architecture: a frozen 2x2 patch-whitening first conv, with whitening computed in prepare from training patches; Dirac init; 3 residual groups of 3 convs at widths 128/384/576; BatchNorm-GELU. Optimizer: Nesterov SGD, lr 9.0 (airbench scaling), wd 0.012, batch size 1024, triangular LR schedule, 9 epochs, label smoothing 0.3. Data: the dataset stays on the GPU in fp16/channels_last; random crop (pad 2) runs on the GPU; derandomized alternating flip. No TTA and no torch.compile yet. Eval is a plain forward pass with no state changes. Build warms up eager kernels and cuDNN on synthetic tensors for train batch 1024 and eval B in {1, 1024}. This is the base recipe every other idea builds on.
ideas.expected: First feasible run: accuracy 0.750-0.765, time 8-13 s, complete=True. If accuracy falls below 0.753, raise to 10 epochs before testing anything else (see the H4.2.1 idea).

ideas.description: On the E-port recipe, change only the epoch count: 9 → 8.5 if the port clears 0.753 with at least 0.3 pp margin, otherwise 9 → 10. Everything else stays identical, so this measures the local accuracy-vs-time slope that sets how far epochs can be cut.
ideas.expected: 8.5 epochs: accuracy drops 0.2-0.5 pp and time drops 4-8%. 10 epochs: accuracy rises about 0.5-0.8 pp and time rises about 11%.

ideas.description: On the port, compile the model's forward+backward with torch.compile (mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs') in build. Compile and warm up on synthetic inputs for the train batch shape and the ragged last-batch shape, and in eval mode for B in {1, 7, 512, 1024} (mark the batch dimension dynamic for eval, or fall back to the eager model for eval). Also replace the per-param SGD loop with a foreach/fused SGD. Math stays unchanged.
ideas.expected: Time drops 10-25% (for example 10 s → 8 s). Accuracy stays within ±0.2 pp. Eval stays under 5 s for every B.

ideas.description: On the port at 9 epochs, add Lookahead/EMA of weights in the airbench96_faster style: update every 5 steps, alpha ramping as in the reference, final weights set to the EMA copy. All EMA state is created and reset in prepare. The forward pass is unchanged.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.2-0.5 pp at under 2% extra time. That margin would later allow cutting about 0.5 epoch.

ideas.description: Re-run the port recipe (or the current best feasible recipe) byte-identically, as a noise calibration. Record the per-seed accuracies from both runs to estimate per-seed std and run-to-run time drift. This sets the margin needed above 0.753 for the 40-seed judgment.
ideas.expected: Mean times within 2% of each other. Per-seed std 0.15-0.4 pp. Mean accuracy differs by under 0.15 pp because the seeds are identical; any difference reflects nondeterminism only.

ideas.description: On the compiled port, drop the ragged last batch, so every training step has the same shape, and verify via warm-up logging that no recompile or autotune happens inside prepare/train. Compare against the compiled port that warmed up only the main shape.
ideas.expected: Time drops by 0.2-0.5 s (about 3-5%) if recompiles were leaking into the timed region; otherwise no change. Accuracy unchanged within 0.1 pp, since only about 0.03 epoch of data is dropped.

ideas.description: Explore. On the port backbone, switch the conv filters to Muon: Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized Nesterov momentum, lr about 0.24, momentum 0.6. Keep SGD for BatchNorm params, whitening bias and the head. Batch size 2000 with the same epoch count. Newton-Schulz runs in bf16 with a foreach-style batched implementation.
ideas.expected: If H1.2 holds, accuracy rises 0.3-1 pp at about equal time, which buys roughly 1 epoch. Risk: worse accuracy at bs 2000 on CIFAR-100, or Newton-Schulz overhead adding over 5% time.

ideas.description: Explore. On the port, apply progressive resizing: the first about 40% of epochs at 24 px, the next 30% at 28 px, the rest at 32 px (random-resized-crop on the GPU via F.interpolate). Warm up every resolution in build on synthetic data. Epoch count unchanged.
ideas.expected: Time drops 5-15%. Accuracy changes between -0.5 and +0.1 pp; a loss above 0.2 pp would refute H2.3.1.

structured_output.summary:
So far there is only the template baseline: accuracy 0.012 at 0.14 s, so the harness adds almost no fixed cost. The queue was empty, so I'm adding 8 ideas and dropping none.

**Run first (priority 5):** port an airbench96-style recipe to test H1.1.1. It keeps the data on the GPU and uses patch-whitening, Dirac init, Nesterov SGD, label smoothing 0.3, alternating flip and 9 epochs. Every other idea builds on this port.

**Exploit ideas:**
- **H4.2.1, priority 4:** change only the epoch count. Go to 8.5 if the port clears 0.753 with margin, or to 10 if it misses.
- **H2.2.1, priority 4:** compile the train step in build and use a fused optimizer.
- **H1.3.2, priority 3:** add Lookahead/EMA of the weights.
- **H4.1.1, priority 3:** re-run the same recipe unchanged to measure seed and timing noise, which sets the safety margin.
- **H3.1.1, priority 3:** drop the ragged last batch so no recompiles happen inside the timed region.

**Explore ideas, priority 2:**
- **H1.2.1:** switch the conv filters to the Muon optimizer.
- **H2.3.1:** train early epochs at lower resolution (progressive resizing).

No uncertainty-committee forecasts were provided, so none of the ideas were reshaped to settle member disagreements.
